requirement: `habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Both outputs build their tables through one renderer, and each output has a test that checks width, alignment, and labels.

**Same renderer.**
- `habeas status` calls `render_evidence_table` in `src/commands.rs`, in `status_markdown_with_github`. That function is reached from the marked `status_markdown_with_options`.
- The mdBook index calls the same `render_evidence_table` in `src/index.rs`, in `DetailPlan::populate`. That call carries its own `{impl}` for this requirement.

**Column widths and alignment.**
- `render_evidence_table` in `src/markdown.rs` computes each column's width as the maximum of the header text and every cell.
- It pads every row, including the header and `---` separator rows, to those widths with `{:<width$}`.
- It is reachable from both `{impl}` items.

**Same evidence-state labels.**
- Both callers pass `evidence.state().label()`, which is `EvidenceState::label` in `src/index.rs`.
- The renderer does not alter the label text.

**Callers may differ (MAY).**
- Status filters definitions by glob, `--all`, and verbose mode. It uses name cells of the form `` `name` (kind) ``.
- The index covers every detail page. It uses linked cells of the form ``[`name`](href) (kind)``.
- The renderer accepts both, because it takes pre-built name cells.

**Tests.**
- `tests/commands.rs::status_tables_align_each_column_to_its_widest_cell` runs `habeas status` and `habeas status --all`. It asserts identical pipe positions on every row, a column width equal to the widest cell, the `---` separator, and the labels Valid, Missing, Determination false, and Invalid.
- `src/index.rs::index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` asserts the same pipe positions and widest-cell widths in the index table. It also asserts the state labels in linked name cells.
- Both tests carry `{test}` references to this requirement.
